about: Asana is a San Francisco work management software company, founded in 2008 by Dustin Moskovitz and Justin Rosenstein. Its platform helps teams plan, track and automate projects and goals, with AI features. Customers are businesses and nonprofits, paying subscriptions, with revenue around 700 million dollars and over 100,000 paying customers in 190 countries. It direct-listed on the NYSE (ASAN) in 2020. It is a B2B brand with good awareness among office workers and has run sports sponsorships.

wiki.title: Asana
wiki.what: Postures in hatha yoga and modern yoga practice
wiki.text: An āsana is a body posture, originally and still a general term for a sitting meditation pose, and later extended in hatha yoga and modern yoga as exercise, to any type of position, adding reclining, standing, inverted, twisting, and balancing poses. The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali define "asana" as "[a position that] is steady and comfortable". Patanjali mentions the ability to sit for extended periods as one of the eight limbs of his system. Asanas are also called yoga poses or yoga postures in English.

wiki.title: Asana, Inc.
wiki.text: Asana, Inc. is an American software company based in San Francisco, California whose flagship Asana service is a web and mobile "work management" platform designed to help teams organize, track, and manage their work. Asana, Inc. was founded in 2008 by Dustin Moskovitz and Justin Rosenstein. The product launched commercially in April 2012. In September 2020, the company was valued at $5.5 billion following its direct listing.

about: monday.com is a Tel Aviv work operating system company, founded in 2012, whose cloud platform lets teams build workflows for project management, CRM, software development and operations. It sells subscriptions to over 245,000 customers in 200 plus industries, with annual revenue above 1 billion dollars. It listed on Nasdaq (MNDY) in 2021. Heavy advertiser, including sports sponsorship, and well known among office and technology workers globally.

wiki.title: Monday.com
wiki.text: Monday.com Ltd. is an Israeli software company based in Tel Aviv. It develops work management software. The platform was launched in 2014 and then relaunched in July 2019.

about: NotCo is a Santiago, Chile food technology company using an AI platform called Giuseppe to create plant-based versions of animal-based foods. Its consumer brands include NotMilk, NotBurger, NotMayo and NotIceCream, sold in Latin America, the US and other markets through retailers such as Whole Foods and Walmart, and it also licenses its AI to food manufacturers like Kraft Heinz. Founded in 2015, it raised about 433 million dollars and was valued at 1.5 billion dollars in 2021. Private. Recognized consumer brand in Latin America.

Zain Group is a Kuwait-based mobile telecoms group with operations in Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Jordan, Bahrain and Sudan, serving about 50 million customers with voice, data, fibre, 5G and enterprise services. It started as MTC in Kuwait and later expanded across Africa, then sold African businesses. Listed on the Boursa Kuwait (ZAIN), with large shareholders including Kuwait's Public Institution for Social Security. Strong consumer brand across the Gulf and a prominent sports and events sponsor in the region.

wiki.title: Zain Group
wiki.text: Mobile Telecommunications Company K.S.C.P. is a Kuwaiti mobile telecommunications company founded on 22 June 1983 in Kuwait as MTC, and later rebranded as Zain in 2007. Zain has a commercial presence in eight countries across the Middle East with 50.9 million active customers as of 31 December 2025. The Vice Chairman and Group CEO is Bader Nasser Al-Kharafi, who was appointed in March 2017.

about: United Internet is a German internet services group based in Montabaur, founded in 1988 by Ralph Dommermuth, who remains its largest shareholder. Its brands include 1&1 (mobile and broadband), IONOS (cloud hosting and web), GMX, WEB.DE (consumer email) and Strato. Customers are millions of consumers and small businesses in Germany and Europe, with revenue of about EUR 6 billion. Listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (UTDI). Consumer brands are household names in Germany.

wiki.title: United Internet
wiki.text: United Internet AG is a global Internet services company headquartered in Montabaur, Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany. The company is structured in two business areas, Access and Applications, and has a total of 16 brands and numerous subsidiaries. The well-known brands under the umbrella of United Internet AG include 1&1, Ionos, Strato, Fasthosts, GMX, WEB.DE and 1&1 Versatel.

about: Zoom is a US video communications software company, based in San Jose, California, founded in 2011 by Eric Yuan. Its platform includes Meetings, Phone, Contact Center, Team Chat, Workplace and AI Companion, sold to enterprises, schools and individuals. It surged during the COVID-19 pandemic and has annual revenue near $4.7 billion. It listed on Nasdaq (ZM) in 2019. Very strong consumer and business brand awareness, and a major corporate advertiser.

Opera is an Oslo-based software company behind the Opera web browser, including the gaming browser Opera GX, Opera Mini, and Opera News, with a growing AI browser strategy. It serves hundreds of millions of monthly users worldwide and earns from search deals, advertising and fintech and gaming services. Its ADSs trade on Nasdaq (OPRA), with a Chinese-led shareholder group holding a controlling stake. It is active in esports and gaming sponsorship. Strong consumer awareness, especially among younger and gaming audiences.

wiki.title: Opera
wiki.what: Art form combining sung text and musical score in a theatrical setting
wiki.text: Opera is a form of Western theatre in which music is a fundamental component and dramatic roles are taken by singers. Such a "work" is typically a collaboration between a composer and a librettist and incorporates a number of the performing arts, such as acting, scenery, costume, and sometimes dance or ballet. The performance is typically given in an opera house, accompanied by an orchestra or smaller musical ensemble, which since the early 19th century has been led by a conductor. Although musical theatre is closely related to opera, the two are considered to be distinct from one another.

wiki.title: Opera (company)
wiki.text: Opera Norway AS is a multinational technology corporation headquartered in Oslo, Norway, with additional offices in Europe, China, and Africa. Opera offers a range of products and services that include PC and mobile web browsers, GameMaker and gaming portals, the Opera News content recommendation products, the Opera Ads platform, and a number of Web3 and e-commerce products and services. Opera is noted for browser innovation and its early adoption of technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), cryptocurrency, and Web3. The company has 296 million monthly active users.

about: Everpure appears to be the new name of Pure Storage, the Santa Clara, California maker of all-flash enterprise data storage systems, including FlashArray and FlashBlade, plus the Evergreen subscription model and Portworx cloud-native storage. Customers are large enterprises, cloud providers and AI data centres buying hardware and subscriptions. Pure Storage listed on the NYSE (PSTG) in 2015 and has revenue near $3 billion. The $529 million shown reflects pre-IPO funding up to 2014. B2B technology brand with modest consumer awareness.
cb_desc: Everpure is an all-flash enterprise storage company...
flags: last funding 2014: check it is still independent and operating

wiki.title: Everpure
wiki.text: Everpure, Inc. is an American publicly traded technology company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, United States. While the company originally focused on developing all-flash data storage hardware and software products, it has since expanded to provide a broader range of data management-related services. This evolution was formalized in February 2026, when the company rebranded as Everpure to reflect its shift toward integrated data management solutions.

about: Elastic is a search and data analytics software company with offices in San Francisco and Amsterdam, listed on the NYSE (ESTC). It created Elasticsearch, Kibana and Logstash, and sells Elastic Cloud and solutions for search, observability and security, used by developers and enterprises. Founded in 2012 around the open source project, it has revenue of about 1.4 billion dollars and over 3,000 employees. B2B developer brand widely known in tech, with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Elastic (company)
wiki.text: Elastic is a Dutch-American software company that provides a platform for enterprise search, observability, and cybersecurity. Its product enables users to search and analyze large-scale data, monitor system performance, and detect anomalies. Originally known as Elasticsearch, the company was founded in 2012 in Amsterdam, Netherlands, and has maintained its operational headquarters in both the Netherlands and San Francisco, California, US. Elastic is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol ESTC.

about: Fortinet is a Sunnyvale, California cybersecurity company, listed on Nasdaq (FTNT), known for its FortiGate firewalls, secure networking (SD-WAN), FortiSASE, endpoint, email and cloud security tools, all built on its own chips and the FortiOS operating system. Customers are enterprises, service providers, governments and small businesses worldwide, buying appliances, software subscriptions and services, with annual revenue of about 6 billion dollars and roughly 13,000 employees. Founded in 2000 by Ken and Michael Xie. Strong B2B brand in IT security circles, with sports and event sponsorship presence in several markets.
flags: listed (IPO status: public); last funding 2004: check it is still independent and operating

wiki.title: Fortinet
wiki.text: Fortinet, Inc. is an American cybersecurity company headquartered in Sunnyvale, California. It develops and sells security products including firewalls, endpoint security and intrusion detection systems. Fortinet has offices in the US, Canada, and UK.

about: HubSpot is a Cambridge, Massachusetts software company, listed on the NYSE (HUBS), that sells a cloud platform for marketing, sales, customer service, content management and operations, anchored on a free CRM. Customers are small and mid-sized businesses, who pay subscriptions across tiers, with more than 250,000 customers in over 120 countries. Founded in 2006 by Brian Halligan and Dharmesh Shah, it has around 8,000 employees and annual revenue above 2.5 billion dollars. It runs the INBOUND conference. Strong B2B brand among marketers and small business owners, with growing global recognition.
flags: listed (IPO status: public); last funding 2012: check it is still independent and operating

wiki.title: HubSpot
wiki.text: HubSpot, Inc. is an American customer relationship management firm operating as an unregistered data broker. It is headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

about: EPAM Systems is a Newtown, Pennsylvania software engineering and digital services company, listed on the NYSE (EPAM), that builds software products, platforms and AI solutions for clients in financial services, healthcare, travel, media and retail. It employs tens of thousands of engineers mostly in Europe and Asia, historically with large teams in Belarus, Ukraine and Russia, which it has restructured since 2022. Annual revenue is about 4.7 billion dollars. Founded in 1993, its customers are large enterprises. Strong B2B brand among technology buyers and developers, with little awareness among consumers.
flags: listed (IPO status: public); last funding 2008: check it is still independent and operating

about: Concord Music Group is a Nashville-based music company covering recorded music, music publishing, theatricals and live production, with a catalogue spanning jazz, classic rock, Broadway and pop. Its labels include Fantasy, Stax, Concord Records and Rounder, and Concord Theatricals holds the rights to shows such as Rodgers and Hammerstein works. It earns royalties from streaming, licensing and live shows. Owned by Genstar Capital, GIC and Concord management, among others. Private. Brand known to the music industry; low consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Concord Music Group
wiki.text: Concord Music Group was an American independent music company based in Beverly Hills, California, with worldwide distribution through Universal Music Group. The company specialized in recordings and music publishing. On April 1, 2015, Concord Music Group merged with Bicycle Music Company to become Concord Bicycle Music.

about: DAZN is a London-based global sports streaming service, offering live and on-demand football, boxing, MMA, NFL, tennis and other sports to subscribers in over 200 markets, plus the Eleven and Foxtel acquisitions. It earns subscription fees and advertising, with annual revenue about GBP 3bn and tens of millions of viewers. Owned by Access Industries, led by Len Blavatnik. Private. A major consumer sports brand holding rights such as the FIFA Club World Cup 2025, and a sponsor of sports properties.

wiki.title: DAZN
wiki.text: DAZN is a British global over-the-top entertainment platform primarily offering sports streaming. Founded in 2007 known as Perform Group via the merger of Premium TV Limited and Inform Group, it is owned by Access Industries, the investment group founded by Sir Len Blavatnik, and is headquartered in London. Shay Segev is DAZN's CEO as of January 2021. The non-executive directors are Lincoln Benet, John Gleasure, Guillaume D’Hauteville, Andrew Cramer, and Danny Townsend. Cramer's and Townsend's appointments followed DAZN's acquisition of Foxtel and Surj Sports $1 billion investment in DAZN respectively.

about: BMG Music Publishing is the music publishing arm of BMG Rights Management, a Berlin-based music company (a Bertelsmann subsidiary, with KKR as co-owner until 2023) that manages publishing rights, recorded music and licensing for artists including Mick Jagger, Kylie Minogue and the Rolling Stones' catalog. Operates offices in over 20 markets, with a large catalog. Customers are songwriters, labels and media users. Known in the music industry, low direct consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Bertelsmann Music Group
wiki.text: Bertelsmann Music Group (BMG) was a division of German media company Bertelsmann. It relaunched as BMG Rights Management after the sale of the majority of its assets to Sony Corporation of America on October 1, 2008.

about: The Walt Disney Company is a Burbank, California-based entertainment conglomerate, founded in 1923, with studios (Disney, Pixar, Marvel, Lucasfilm, 20th Century), media networks (ABC, ESPN, National Geographic), streaming (Disney+, Hulu, ESPN+) and parks, experiences and products (Disney parks, cruise line, consumer products). Revenue is about $90 billion. Listed on NYSE (DIS). Among the most recognised consumer brands in the world, and a partner of F1 through ESPN and Star broadcast deals.

wiki.title: The Walt Disney Company
wiki.text: The Walt Disney Company (TWDC), commonly known as Disney, is an American multinational mass media and entertainment conglomerate headquartered at the Walt Disney Studios complex in Burbank, California. Founded on October 16, 1923, by brothers Walt and Roy O. Disney as the Disney Brothers Cartoon Studio, the company later operated under the names Walt Disney Studio and Walt Disney Productions before adopting its current name in 1986. Disney established itself as a leader in animation with the release of Steamboat Willie in 1928. The short film's pioneering use of synchronized sound helped popularize Mickey Mouse, who became the company's masco

about: Comcast is a US media and technology conglomerate headquartered in Philadelphia and listed on Nasdaq (CMCSA). It owns Xfinity broadband and cable, NBCUniversal (NBC, Peacock, Universal Pictures, theme parks, Telemundo), Sky in Europe, and the Versant cable spin-off planned for 2026. It has over 30 million broadband customers and revenue near 120 billion dollars. Money comes from subscriptions, advertising, film and theme park admissions. Huge consumer brands and a major sports broadcaster, including NFL, Premier League and the Olympics, so a likely media partner.

wiki.title: Comcast
wiki.what: American multinational telecommunications and media conglomerate
wiki.text: Comcast is an American multinational mass media, telecommunications, and entertainment conglomerate. Comcast's corporate headquarters is at the Comcast Center in Philadelphia, while NBCUniversal, Comcast's New York operations and other major Comcast assets are headquartered at 30 Rockefeller Plaza in Midtown Manhattan in New York City. The company was ranked 51st in the Forbes Global 2000 in 2023. It is the fourth-largest telecommunications company by worldwide revenue, after AT&T, Verizon, and China Mobile. Comcast is the third-largest pay-TV company, the second-largest cable TV company by subscribers, and the largest home Internet service p

about: Legendary Entertainment is a Burbank-based film, television and media company founded in 2000 by Thomas Tull and owned by China's Dalian Wanda Group since 2016. It produces and co-finances blockbusters such as Dune, Godzilla and Kong, the Jurassic World series (as financing partner), plus the Legendary Comics and television arms. Customers are studios, streamers and audiences; revenue comes from film, licensing and distribution. Strong entertainment brand with a track record of branded content partnerships.

wiki.title: Legendary Entertainment
wiki.text: Legendary Entertainment, LLC is an American mass media company based in Burbank, California. It was founded by film producer Thomas Tull in 2003 after he was fired from Convex Group. The company has often collaborated with the major studios, including Warner Bros. Pictures, Universal Pictures, Sony Pictures, and Paramount Pictures, as well as streaming services such as Netflix and Hulu.

about: United Group is a multi-play telecoms and media provider in Southeast Europe, headquartered in Hoofddorp in the Netherlands and controlled by BC Partners. It operates mobile, broadband and pay-TV in Serbia (SBB), Bulgaria (Vivacom), Slovenia, Croatia, Montenegro and Bosnia, and owns N1 news and Nova TV channels plus sports rights. Millions of subscribers across the Balkans. Privately held, with debt-financed acquisitions. Strong regional consumer brand and sports broadcaster, so a potential media partner.
cb_desc: United Group is the multi-play telecoms and media provider.

wiki.title: United Group
wiki.what: Southeastern European telecom and mass media company
wiki.text: United Group B.V. is a multinational telecommunications and media conglomerate, based in Hoofddorp, Netherlands, that operates across Southeast Europe.

about: Universal Music Group is the world's largest music company, headquartered in Hilversum, Netherlands with major offices in Santa Monica and New York, and listed on Euronext Amsterdam (UMG). Its labels include Republic, Interscope, Island, Capitol, Def Jam and Deutsche Grammophon, with artists such as Taylor Swift, Drake and Billie Eilish, plus Universal Music Publishing and merchandise. Revenue is around 11 billion euros from streaming, licensing and live. Founded 1934 as Decca. Highly visible entertainment brand relevant to artist and music partnerships.

wiki.title: Universal Music Group
wiki.text: Universal Music Group N.V. is a Dutch-American music corporation under Dutch law. While UMG's corporate headquarters are located in Hilversum, Netherlands, its operational headquarters are located in Santa Monica, California. As the biggest music company in the world, it is one of the "Big Three" record labels, along with Sony Music Entertainment and Warner Music Group. Tencent acquired ten percent of Universal Music Group in March 2020 for €3 billion and acquired an additional ten percent stake in January 2021. Pershing Square Holdings later acquired ten percent of UMG before its IPO on the Euronext Amsterdam stock exchange. The French Bollo

about: Cirsa is a Spanish gaming and leisure group headquartered in Terrassa, Catalonia, operating casinos, slot arcades, betting shops, bingo halls and online gaming in Spain, Italy, Latin America and Morocco, with revenue above 2 billion euros. Controlled by Blackstone since 2018 and listed on the Spanish stock exchange since 2025. Founded 1978 by the Lao family. Customers are casino and betting patrons. Strong gaming consumer brand in Spain, though advertising of gambling is restricted there.

Take-Two Interactive is a video game publisher and developer behind the Rockstar Games (Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption) and 2K labels (NBA 2K, WWE 2K, Borderlands, Civilization), plus Zynga mobile games acquired in 2022. Customers are gamers worldwide, with revenue of about $5.5 billion to $6 billion from game sales, in-game purchases and subscriptions. Headquartered in New York. Listed on Nasdaq (TTWO). Games are global consumer brands, with GTA among the best-selling franchises.

wiki.title: Take-Two Interactive
wiki.text: Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. is an American video game holding company based in New York City co-founded by Ryan Brant and Mark E. Seremet in September 1993.

about: Cologix is a North American network-neutral data centre and interconnection operator, with facilities in markets such as Columbus, Dallas, Minneapolis, Montreal, Toronto and Vancouver, where enterprises, cloud providers and carriers connect and house equipment. Headquartered in Denver, Colorado. Revenue comes from colocation, interconnection and cloud connectivity fees. Owned by infrastructure investor Stonepeak. Crunchbase shows about $2.7 billion in funding, mainly financing. Private. B2B infrastructure brand with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Cologix
wiki.text: Cologix, a network neutral interconnection and data center company, runs 45+ interconnection locations across 13 North American markets. The edge markets that Cologix operates in are: Ashburn, Virginia; Calgary, Alberta; Columbus, Ohio; Dallas, Texas; Jacksonville, Florida; Lakeland, Florida; Minneapolis, Minnesota; Montreal, Quebec; Silicon Valley, California; Toronto, Ontario; Northern New Jersey; and Vancouver, British Columbia. The company supports eight Internet exchanges.

about: London-listed gambling company Evoke PLC, formerly 888 Holdings, owner of William Hill, 888 Casino and Mr Green. HQ in the input shows Herzliya, Israel. Customers are UK and European bettors. Strong consumer brands in the UK, with sports betting sponsorship. Evoke is a large betting and gaming operator, with revenue of about GBP 1.7 billion. Its brands appear on sports shirts and advertising.

TKO Group Holdings is the US sports and entertainment company formed in 2023 by combining UFC and WWE under Endeavor's control, listed on the NYSE (TKO). It owns the Ultimate Fighting Championship, World Wrestling Entertainment, PBR (bull riding) and the Zuffa Boxing venture, and earns revenue from media rights, live events, sponsorships and licensing. Based in New York, with Endeavor as majority owner, and combined revenue of around 3 billion dollars or more. Large global fan base and heavy sponsorship activity, making it a peer sports property as well as a potential partner.

wiki.title: TKO Group Holdings
wiki.text: TKO Group Holdings, Inc. (TKO) is an American sports and entertainment company. Established on September 12, 2023, the public company was formed by a merger between Endeavor subsidiary Zuffa—the parent company of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC), a mixed martial arts promotion—and the professional wrestling promotion World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE).

about: Merlin Entertainments is a UK leisure group based in Poole, Dorset, operating Legoland parks, Madame Tussauds, SEA LIFE aquariums, the London Eye, Alton Towers and Gardaland, with over 140 attractions in 25 countries. It was taken private in 2019 by Kirkbi (owner of Lego), Blackstone and CPPIB. Visitors are families and tourists. Strong consumer brand visibility worldwide.

wiki.title: Merlin Entertainments
wiki.text: Merlin Entertainments Limited is a global entertainment company based in London, England, which operates a number of theme park resorts and other visitor attractions. It is currently owned by the consortium Motion JVCO Ltd, which includes Kirkbi, Blackstone Inc and CPP Investments.

about: Singapore-headquartered group that owns Shopee e-commerce, Garena gaming (Free Fire) and SeaMoney fintech, serving Southeast Asia, Taiwan and Brazil. Founded in 2009 by Forrest Li. Listed on the NYSE (SE). Revenue around USD 20 billion. Consumer brands with very high awareness in Southeast Asia and heavy sports advertising.

wiki.title: Sea Ltd
wiki.text: Sea Limited is a tech conglomerate headquartered in Singapore. It is listed on the New York Stock Exchange, with revenue of US$16.8 billion (2024). Sea currently functions as a holding company for Garena, Monee and Shopee, the largest e-commerce platform in Southeast Asia.

wiki.title: Sea
wiki.text: A sea is a very large body of salty water. The term has two distinct meanings. The first is the interconnected body of seawater that spans most of Earth, known as the sea or the ocean. The second is a named body of water: usually either a marginal sea, or a large, nearly landlocked body of water.

about: TelevisaUnivision is a Mexican-American Spanish-language media company formed in 2022 by merging Televisa's content assets with Univision, headquartered in Miami, Florida (with major operations in Mexico City), operating networks, local stations, ViX streaming, and production, and reaching Hispanic audiences in the US, Mexico and Latin America. Revenue is around $5 billion. Owned by Searchlight, Grupo Televisa and others. Very strong consumer brands with major football broadcast rights.

wiki.title: TelevisaUnivision
wiki.text: TelevisaUnivision is a Mexican–American media company that owns American Spanish-language broadcast network Univision and free-to-air channels in Mexico such as Las Estrellas, 5*, N+ Foro, and NU9VE alongside a collection of specialty television channels and production studios. Forty-five percent (45%) of the company is held by the Mexican telecommunications and broadcasting company Grupo Televisa, which was a major programming partner for Univision until the company sold their content assets to Univision Communications in 2022.

about: Beast Industries is the media and consumer business of YouTuber MrBeast (Jimmy Donaldson), based in Greenville, North Carolina. It produces his YouTube videos and the Amazon show Beast Games, and owns Feastables snacks and chocolate, Lunchly lunch kits and other ventures, plus the MrBeast Burger brand. His main channel has several hundred million subscribers. It has raised investment at a reported valuation of about 5 billion dollars. It is a hugely visible youth consumer brand and a major advertising platform.

wiki.title: MrBeast
wiki.text: James Stephen "Jimmy" Donaldson, better known as MrBeast, is an American YouTuber, internet personality, entrepreneur, and philanthropist. He is the founder of Beast Industries, a conglomerate that holds various media channels, MrBeast Burger, Feastables, Lunchly, and more. He produces high-paced YouTube videos built around elaborate challenges and philanthropic efforts that are noted for their high production values. With more than 526 million subscribers, his main channel is the most subscribed on YouTube. He is also the third most followed account on TikTok.

about: Playtika is a mobile games developer and publisher known for free-to-play social casino and casual titles such as Slotomania, Bingo Blitz, House of Fun, Caesars Slots and Board Kings, with players in many countries. It earns revenue from in-app purchases and advertising, with annual revenue near 2.5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Herzliya, Israel, with studios worldwide, it has been controlled by a Chinese-led consortium since 2016 and listed on Nasdaq (PLTK) in 2021. Large reach among casual gamers, though the company brand itself is little known.

wiki.title: Playtika
wiki.text: Playtika Holding Corp. is an Israeli digital entertainment company specializing in the development and publication of mobile games. In 2021, Playtika had over 35 million monthly active users.

about: Cirque du Soleil is a Canadian entertainment company founded in 1984 in Quebec, producing touring and resident live acrobatic shows such as O, Mystere, Kooza and Corteo in Las Vegas and around the world. Customers are ticket-buying audiences and corporate clients for events. Based in Montreal, with thousands of artists and staff. It restructured through bankruptcy in 2020 and passed to its lenders. Highly recognised consumer brand in much of the world.

wiki.title: Cirque du Soleil
wiki.text: The Cirque du Soleil Entertainment Group, commonly known as Cirque du Soleil, is a Canadian entertainment company and the largest contemporary circus producer in the world. Headquartered in the inner-city area of Saint-Michel, Montreal, it was founded in Baie-Saint-Paul on 16 June 1984 by former street performers Guy Laliberté and Gilles Ste-Croix.

about: Ooredoo is a Qatar-based telecoms group, majority owned by the Qatar Investment Authority, which provides mobile, fixed, broadband and enterprise services across the Middle East, North Africa and Southeast Asia, including Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Iraq, Indonesia (Indosat) and Maldives, with about 100 million customers. Revenue is about $9 billion. Listed on the Qatar Stock Exchange (ORDS). Strong consumer brand across the region and an active sports sponsor.

wiki.title: Ooredoo
wiki.text: Ooredoo Q.P.S.C.,, is a Qatari state-owned multinational telecommunications company headquartered in Doha. Ooredoo provides mobile, wireless, wireline, and content services with market share in domestic and international telecommunication markets and in business and residential markets.

about: FC Barcelona is the Spanish football club, founded in 1899, one of the most followed sports brands in the world, with hundreds of millions of fans. Based in Barcelona, it earns revenue from matchday, broadcasting, commercial deals and merchandise, of about EUR 800 million a year. A member-owned club, with sponsors including Spotify, Nike and Beko. Huge global consumer profile and already a major sponsorship property.

wiki.title: FC Barcelona
wiki.text: Futbol Club Barcelona, commonly known as FC Barcelona and colloquially as Barça, is a professional football club based in Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain, that competes in La Liga, the top division of Spanish football.

about: Pearson is a British education company based in London, selling digital learning, assessments, qualifications (Edexcel), English language learning (Pearson Test of English, Versant), textbooks and the virtual schools and workforce skills. It serves schools, universities, governments and professionals, mostly in the US, UK and Asia, with revenue near 3.5 billion pounds. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (PSON) and a FTSE 100 company, with roots in 1844. Well-known education brand; a former owner of the Financial Times and Penguin.

Sonos is a consumer audio company based in Santa Barbara, California, selling wireless multi-room speakers, soundbars, subwoofers, headphones such as Ace, and a music app that streams from services like Spotify and Apple Music. It sells through retailers and its own website in more than 50 countries, with revenue around US$1.5 billion. Founded in 2002, it listed on Nasdaq in 2018 (SONO). Strong premium consumer brand recognised globally, with a design-led image that suits partnership and entertainment tie-ins.

wiki.title: Sonos
wiki.text: Sonos, Inc. is an American audio equipment manufacturer headquartered in Santa Barbara, California. The company was founded in 2002 by John MacFarlane, Craig Shelburne, Tom Cullen, and Trung Mai.

about: Ubisoft is a French video game publisher and developer based near Paris, behind franchises such as Assassin's Creed, Far Cry, Rainbow Six, Just Dance, The Division and Prince of Persia, with studios in over 30 countries and about 18,000 staff. Listed on Euronext Paris (UBI). Revenue is roughly 2 billion euros a year. In 2025 it set up a subsidiary with backing from Tencent. Strong global consumer brand with an extensive esports and sponsorship footprint.

wiki.title: Ubisoft
wiki.text: Ubisoft Entertainment SA is a French video game publisher headquartered in Saint-Mandé with development studios across the world. Its video game franchises include Anno, Assassin's Creed, Driver, Far Cry, Just Dance, Prince of Persia, Rabbids, Rayman, Tom Clancy's, and Watch Dogs.

about: Global entertainment group, formerly FL Entertainment, that combined with Banijay Entertainment in 2024. It produces and distributes television formats and programmes such as Survivor, Big Brother, MasterChef and Peaky Blinders, with more than 100 production companies across many countries, and also owns the Betclic sports betting and gaming business in France and Europe. Based in Paris and listed on Euronext Amsterdam. Customers are broadcasters, streamers and bettors. Strong content brand among industry buyers, and Betclic is a visible sports sponsor in Europe.

wiki.title: Banijay Group
wiki.text: Banijay Group N.V. is a French entertainment holding company based in Paris, France, and legally incorporated in Amsterdam, Netherlands. It was formed in May 2022 from a merger with special-purpose acquisition company (SPAC) Pegasus Entrepreneurs, which saw independent television production group Banijay and online sports betting group Betclic go public.

about: Iliad is a French telecom group, founded by Xavier Niel and based in Paris, behind the Free mobile and broadband brand in France, plus Iliad Italia, Play in Poland and a stake in other operators. It serves over 50 million subscribers, with revenue around EUR 11bn, and owns data center and fibre assets, including OpCore. Privately held, controlled by Niel's holding after delisting in 2018. Free is a strong disruptive consumer brand in France.

wiki.title: Iliad
wiki.text: The Iliad is one of two major surviving ancient Greek epic poems, along with the Odyssey, attributed to Homer. It is one of the oldest extant works of literature still widely read by modern readers. Like the Odyssey, the poem is divided into 24 books and was written in dactylic hexameter. It contains 15,693 lines in its standard edition. The Iliad is often regarded as the first substantial piece of European literature and is central to the study of classical philology.

wiki.title: Iliad SA
wiki.text: Iliad SA, stylized as iliad, is a French telecommunications company. It is based in Paris and its operations comprise fixed and mobile telephony services, prepaid phone cards and Internet access providing and hosting services.

about: Verizon is a US telecom giant, based in Basking Ridge, New Jersey, serving about 145 million mobile and broadband connections with wireless, Fios fibre, 5G home internet and business services. It earns subscription fees and has revenue near $135bn. Listed on the NYSE and Nasdaq (VZ). Very strong consumer brand and a major sports sponsor, notably as an NFL partner and in IndyCar. Funding figure shown reflects debt raised rather than venture equity.

wiki.title: Verizon
wiki.text: Verizon Communications Inc. is an American telecommunications company headquartered in New York City. It is the world's second-largest telecommunications company by revenue and its mobile network is the largest wireless carrier in the United States, with 146.8 million subscribers as of March 31, 2026. The company was founded as Bell Atlantic Corporation and renamed to Verizon on June 30, 2000 as a result of a merger with GTE.

about: Princeton Digital Group is a Singapore-based data center developer and operator with campuses in Singapore, China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia and Thailand serving cloud and internet customers. It is backed by Warburg Pincus and Macquarie Asset Management and has raised billions in equity and debt. Private, founded in 2017. B2B infrastructure, with no consumer awareness.

Prysmian Group is a Milan-based Italian cable maker, the world's largest by revenue, producing power transmission, submarine, building and telecom cables and optical fibre for utilities, offshore wind, data center and construction customers worldwide. Revenue is about EUR 17-18bn with over 30,000 employees. It acquired Encore Wire in the US in 2024. Listed on Borsa Italiana (PRY). B2B industrial brand with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Prysmian Group
wiki.text: Prysmian S.p.A. is a multinational company with headquarters in Milan, Italy, specializing in the production of electrical cables for use in the energy and telecom sectors and for optical fibres. Prysmian is in Europe with 48 plants, 23 in North America, 13 in LATAM, 13 APAC, 7 MEAT.

about: Singtel is Singapore's largest telecom operator, majority-owned by Temasek, selling mobile, broadband, TV and enterprise ICT services in Singapore and through associates such as Optus (Australia), Airtel (India), Telkomsel (Indonesia) and Globe. It also invests in data centers via Nxera. Revenue is about S$14bn. Listed on the Singapore Exchange (Z74). Very strong consumer brand in Singapore, and a past title sponsor of the Singapore Grand Prix.

wiki.title: Singtel
wiki.text: Singapore Telecommunications Limited, trading as Singtel, is a Singaporean telecommunications conglomerate. It is Singapore's principal fixed-line operator and one of the four major mobile network operators operating in the country.

about: Telecom Italia (TIM) is Italy's former state telephone monopoly, based in Milan. It operates fixed and mobile telecom services and ICT for consumers and businesses in Italy, and owns a major stake in the Brazilian operator TIM Brasil. In 2024 it sold its fixed network (NetCo) to KKR; the brand TIM remains. Listed on Borsa Italiana (TIT). Customers are tens of millions of mobile lines. Very high brand awareness in Italy and sponsor of football (Serie A) and cycling.

wiki.title: TIM Group
wiki.text: TIM S.p.A.,, is an Italian multinational telecommunications company with headquarters in Rome, Milan, Bari, and Naples, which provides fixed, public and mobile telephony, and DSL data services.

about: Swisscom is Switzerland's leading telecom company, headquartered in Worblaufen near Bern and listed on SIX Swiss Exchange (SCMN), with the Swiss Confederation holding the majority. It provides mobile, broadband, TV (blue TV) and IT services to consumers and businesses, owns Fastweb in Italy after acquiring Vodafone Italia in 2024, and employs about 20,000 people with revenue near 11 billion francs. Founded 1998. Very strong Swiss consumer brand and active sports sponsor.

wiki.title: Swisscom
wiki.text: Swisscom AG is a major telecommunications provider in Switzerland. Its headquarters are in Worblaufen, near Bern. The Swiss government owns 51% of Swisscom. According to its own published data, Swisscom's market shares in Switzerland are 56% for mobile, 50% for broadband and 37% for TV telecommunications. Its Italian subsidiary, Fastweb, has 16% share of the private broadband market and 29% of the corporate broadband market. It is also active in the mobile market.

about: Zain Saudi Arabia (Mobile Telecommunications Company Saudi Arabia) is a Riyadh-based mobile operator, part of the Kuwait-founded Zain Group, serving consumers and businesses with mobile, broadband and 5G services. Listed on the Saudi Exchange, it holds a large licence base. Customers are Saudi subscribers. Established consumer telecom brand in the Kingdom, with active sports and event sponsorships regionally.
cb_desc: Zain was established as a leading telecom provider in th...

wiki.title: Zain Saudi Arabia
wiki.text: Mobile Telecommunication Company Saudi Arabia is a Saudi Arabian telecommunications and digital services company that provides telecom services, 5G network, digital payment services, cloud computing, IoT solutions, fiber services, drones under the brand name Zain LPU. It is part of the Zain Group, a Kuwaiti telecommunications company.

about: Nairobi-based telecom operator, owned about 55 percent by Bharti Airtel, providing mobile and mobile-money services to about 160 million customers in 14 African countries. Listed in London and Lagos. Revenue is about $5 billion. Strong consumer brand across Africa and sponsor of football. Airtel Africa has operations in Nigeria, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Zambia and others, and is a significant sponsor of cricket and football on the continent.

wiki.title: Airtel Africa
wiki.text: Airtel Africa plc is a British company that provides telecommunications and mobile money services in 14 countries in Africa, mainly in East, Central and West Africa. Airtel Africa is majority owned by the Indian telecommunications company Bharti Airtel. Airtel Africa offers mobile voice and data services as well as mobile money services both nationally and internationally. Airtel Nigeria is the most profitable unit of Airtel Africa, due to its cheap data plans in Nigeria. As of March 2019, Airtel had over 99 million subscribers in the continent. It is listed on the London Stock Exchange and is a constituent of the FTSE 100 Index.

about: Singapore-based eSIM marketplace letting travellers buy mobile data plans for over 200 countries through an app, without swapping SIM cards. Customers are international travellers, with a growing B2B offering. Founded 2019 and has raised roughly USD 287 million, valued above USD 1 billion. Consumer app with strong awareness among frequent travellers and heavy digital advertising.

wiki.title: Airalo
wiki.text: Airalo is a telecommunications company founded in 2019 by Ahmet Bahadir Özdemir and Abraham Burak, and sells eSIMs. It is headquartered in Delaware, with its operational base in Singapore. As of July 2025, the company reported over 20 million users. Airalo provides eSIM services compatible with mobile networks in most countries, and users can choose between eSIMs for a specific destination, for a region, and at a global level, with various data packages available, including unlimited data eSIMs.

about: China Mobile is the world's largest mobile operator by subscribers, with around a billion mobile customers, plus broadband, 5G, cloud and data services in China. It is majority owned by the Chinese state through China Mobile Communications Group, with a Hong Kong listing (0941) and a Shanghai listing (600941). Its headquarters are in Beijing, with the Hong Kong office shown here. Revenue is about 130 billion dollars. It is a hugely visible consumer brand in China, with extensive advertising and sports sponsorship.

wiki.title: China Mobile
wiki.text: China Mobile is the trade name of both China Mobile Limited, and its ultimate controlling shareholder, China Mobile Communications Group Co., Ltd., a Chinese state-owned telecommunications company. It provides mobile voice and multimedia services through its nationwide mobile telecommunications network across mainland China and Hong Kong. China Mobile is the largest wireless carrier in China, with 945.50 million subscribers as of June 2021. China Mobile was ranked #25 in Forbes' Global 2000 in 2023.

about: ZTE is a Chinese telecommunications equipment and technology company based in Shenzhen, selling 4G and 5G network equipment, fibre access, routers, and consumer devices such as smartphones (nubia, ZTE Axon) to carriers in over 160 countries. It is listed in Shenzhen (000063) and Hong Kong (0763), with tens of thousands of employees, and revenue above 100 billion yuan. Founded in 1985. Known in telecom circles and with some consumer awareness, and has used sports sponsorship.

wiki.title: ZTE
wiki.text: ZTE Corporation is a Chinese partially state-owned technology company that specializes in telecommunication. Founded in 1985, ZTE is listed on both the Hong Kong and Shenzhen Stock Exchanges.

about: Prysmian is an Italian multinational cable maker (Prysmian Group) headquartered in Milan, listed on Borsa Italiana, producing power, telecom and submarine cables for energy, construction and communications. The input shows its US base in Franklin Park, Illinois. It employs around 30,000 people and has revenue of about 17 billion euros. B2B brand with low consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Prysmian Group
wiki.text: Prysmian S.p.A. is a multinational company with headquarters in Milan, Italy, specializing in the production of electrical cables for use in the energy and telecom sectors and for optical fibres. Prysmian is in Europe with 48 plants, 23 in North America, 13 in LATAM, 13 APAC, 7 MEAT.

about: Chinese consumer electronics and internet company producing smartphones, smart home devices, TVs, wearables, and electric cars (SU7 and YU7), run on its HyperOS and IoT platform. Sells to mass-market consumers through online and retail stores in over 100 countries and earns from hardware plus internet services, with revenue above 50 billion dollars. Headquartered in Beijing; founded 2010 by Lei Jun. Listed in Hong Kong (1810). Well-known value brand in Asia, Europe and emerging markets, with substantial marketing budgets and sports sponsorships.

wiki.title: Xiaomi
wiki.text: Xiaomi is a Chinese multinational corporation and technology company headquartered in Beijing, China. It is best known for its consumer electronics, software, and electric vehicles. It is the third-largest smartphone seller in the world as of 2025, behind Apple and Samsung, most of which run on the Xiaomi HyperOS operating system. It has 754.1 million global monthly active users, as of December 2025. The company is ranked 232nd and is the youngest company on the Fortune Global 500. It has been called the "Apple of China".

about: Korean electronics giant making smartphones (Galaxy), TVs, home appliances, memory chips and display panels, sold to consumers and businesses worldwide. Revenue is roughly 200 to 250 billion dollars with about 260,000 employees. Headquartered in Seoul; founded 1969 and the flagship of the Samsung group. Listed on the Korea Exchange (005930). One of the world's most recognised consumer brands, with a long record as a global sponsor of the Olympics, football and other sports.

wiki.title: Samsung Electronics
wiki.text: Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. is a South Korean multinational consumer electronics and semiconductor corporation founded in 1969 and headquartered in Yeongtong District, Suwon, South Korea. It is the flagship listed company of the Samsung chaebol and a major supplier of memory chips, displays, smartphones and home appliances.

about: Franco-Italian semiconductor maker selling microcontrollers, sensors, power chips, silicon carbide devices and MEMS to carmakers and industrial and consumer electronics firms; Apple and Tesla are well-known customers. Revenue of about 13 to 17 billion dollars and roughly 50,000 employees. Legal seat in Geneva (Plan-les-Ouates), operations in Italy and France; formed in 1987 by SGS and Thomson. Listed in Paris, Milan and New York (STM). B2B component brand with low consumer awareness, though it has sponsored motorsport and Formula E.

wiki.title: STMicroelectronics
wiki.text: STMicroelectronics NV is a European multinational semiconductor contract manufacturing and design company. It is the largest of such companies in Europe. The company is incorporated in the Netherlands and headquartered in Plan-les-Ouates, Switzerland. It manufactures a wide range of microelectronics, including the widely used STM8 and STM32 microcontrollers.

about: Foxconn Technology Group, formally Hon Hai Precision Industry, is the world's largest electronics contract manufacturer, assembling iPhones for Apple and servers, including for Nvidia AI, as well as electric vehicles through Foxtron and EV platforms. Revenue near 200 billion dollars and over 1 million employees, with plants in China, India, Vietnam, Mexico and the US. Headquartered in New Taipei City; founded 1974 by Terry Gou. Listed in Taipei (2317). B2B manufacturer, little consumer brand awareness.

wiki.title: Foxconn
wiki.text: Hon Hai Precision Industry Co., Ltd. (鴻海精密工業股份有限公司), doing business as Hon Hai Technology Group (鴻海科技集團) in Taiwan, Foxconn Technology Group (富士康科技集团) in China, and Foxconn (富士康) internationally, is a Taiwanese multinational electronics contract manufacturer established in 1974 with headquarters in Tucheng District, New Taipei City, Taiwan. In 2023, the company's annual revenue reached 6.16 trillion New Taiwan dollars and was ranked 20th in the 2023 Fortune Global 500. It is the world's largest contract manufacturer of electronics. While headquartered in Taiwan, the company earns the majority of its revenue from assets in China and is one of

about: South Korean maker of display panels, notably OLED and LCD screens for TVs, smartphones, monitors, laptops and cars, supplying LG Electronics, Apple, and automotive customers. Revenue near 20 trillion won. Headquartered in Seoul (Yeouido); established in 1985 as a joint venture, spun out in 1999 from LG. Listed on the Korea Exchange (034220) and New York (LPL), with LG Corp as the main shareholder. B2B component brand with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: LG Display
wiki.text: LG Display Co., Ltd. is one of the world's largest manufacturers and supplier of thin-film transistor liquid crystal display (TFT-LCD) panels, OLEDs and flexible displays. LG Display is headquartered in Seoul, South Korea, and currently operates nine fabrication facilities and seven back-end assembly facilities in South Korea, China, Poland and Mexico.

about: Analog Devices designs analog, mixed-signal and digital signal processing chips for industrial automation, automotive, communications, healthcare and consumer devices, after acquiring Maxim Integrated in 2021. Revenue near 10 billion dollars. Headquartered in Wilmington, Massachusetts; founded 1965. Listed on Nasdaq (ADI). B2B component brand, strong among engineers and automotive suppliers, with limited consumer visibility; it has sponsored Formula 1 teams.

wiki.title: Analog Devices
wiki.text: Analog Devices, Inc. (ADI), also known simply as Analog, is an American multinational semiconductor company specializing in data conversion, signal processing, and power management technology, headquartered in Wilmington, Massachusetts.

about: Emirates Global Aluminium is the largest industrial company in the UAE outside oil and gas and one of the largest aluminium producers in the world, with smelters in Abu Dhabi and Dubai and a US project in Oklahoma. Sells primary aluminium to manufacturers in automotive, aerospace, construction and packaging. Headquartered in Dubai; formed 2013 from Dubai Aluminium and Emirates Aluminium. Owned equally by Mubadala and the Investment Corporation of Dubai. B2B with low consumer visibility, but it has sports sponsorship links.

wiki.title: Emirates Global Aluminium
wiki.text: Emirates Global Aluminium (EGA) is an aluminium conglomerate with interests in bauxite/alumina and primary aluminium smelting. A state-owned enterprise, it is jointly controlled by the Mubadala Investment Company and the Investment Corporation of Dubai, sovereign wealth funds of the United Arab Emirates.

about: Wesco International is a business-to-business distributor of electrical, industrial and communications products and supply chain services, serving utilities, data centers, construction and industrial customers in the US, Canada and beyond. Revenue near 22 billion dollars. Headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania; roots to 1922 as Westinghouse Electric Supply. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (WCC) and acquired Anixter in 2020. B2B brand with low consumer awareness.

wiki.title: WESCO International
wiki.text: Wesco International, Inc. is a publicly traded American holding company for Wesco Distribution, an electrical distribution and services company based in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

about: Ceconomy is the German parent of consumer electronics retailers MediaMarkt and Saturn, which run hundreds of stores in Europe, with an online and services business. Revenue near 23 billion euros. Headquartered in Dusseldorf; separated from Metro in 2017. Listed in Frankfurt (CEC). China's JD.com agreed in 2025 to acquire Ceconomy for roughly 2.2 billion euros. MediaMarkt and Saturn are well-known consumer brands across Europe with a history of football and sports sponsorship.

wiki.title: Ceconomy
wiki.text: Ceconomy AG is an international retail company headquartered in Düsseldorf, Germany. Its history goes back to the Metro Group. Ceconomy operates more than 1,000 consumer electronics stores in eleven countries. In addition to MediaMarkt and Saturn, the group owns Deutsche Technikberatung. Approximately 24 % of its sales are generated online.

about: Lowe's is the second-largest US home improvement retailer, headquartered in Mooresville, North Carolina. It operates about 1,700 stores in the US and Canada selling appliances, tools, building materials, hardware, lawn and garden products and home decor, to homeowners, DIY customers and professional contractors, online and in store. Annual revenue is around $80-85bn with roughly 300,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE (LOW). Very high consumer brand visibility in North America and a long-time major sports sponsor, notably NASCAR, where it has been a headline sponsor of Hendrick Motorsports.

wiki.title: Lowe's
wiki.what: American home improvement and hardware store chain
wiki.text: Lowe's Companies, Inc. is an American retail company specializing in home improvement. Headquartered in Mooresville, North Carolina, the company operates a chain of retail stores in the United States. As of October 28, 2022, Lowe's and its related businesses operated 2,181 home improvement and hardware stores in North America.

about: Nidec Corporation is a Kyoto-headquartered Japanese maker of electric motors, one of the world's largest. It produces precision small motors for hard drives, appliances and cars, plus automotive traction motors, e-axles, robotics, industrial and appliance motors and machine tools, with revenue of roughly JPY 2.3 trillion and over 100,000 staff across more than 40 countries. Customers are automakers, electronics firms and industrial companies. Listed in Tokyo (6594) and on the NYSE until delisting there. Largely B2B, well known in industry but little consumer visibility.

wiki.title: Nidec
wiki.text: Nidec Corporation , formerly known as Nippon Densan Corporation , is a Japanese manufacturer and distributor of electric motors. Its products are found in hard-disk drives, electric appliances, automobiles and commercial and manufacturing equipment. The company is the global market leader for the spindle motors that power hard-disk drives.

about: Electrolux is a Stockholm-based Swedish appliance maker, selling refrigerators, ovens, washing machines, dishwashers, vacuum cleaners and air purifiers under Electrolux, AEG, Frigidaire and Westinghouse brands to consumers across Europe, North and Latin America, Asia and Australia. Revenue is about SEK 130bn and it employs around 45,000 people, with manufacturing in many countries. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (ELUX B). Large household-name brand with strong visibility in Europe, and active in sports and F1-adjacent sponsorships in some markets.

wiki.title: Electrolux
wiki.text: Electrolux AB is a Swedish multinational home appliance manufacturer, headquartered in Stockholm. It is consistently ranked the world's second largest appliance maker by units sold, after Whirlpool.

about: MediaTek is a Taiwanese fabless semiconductor company based in Hsinchu, designing system-on-chips for smartphones (Dimensity), tablets, smart TVs, Wi-Fi routers, IoT devices, Chromebooks and cars. It sells to phone and electronics makers including Xiaomi, Oppo, Vivo and Samsung, and is the largest smartphone chip supplier by volume. Annual revenue is about NT$ 530bn, with over 20,000 employees. Listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (2454). Mostly B2B, though its logo appears on devices and it has sponsored sport and F1-adjacent campaigns.

wiki.title: MediaTek
wiki.text: MediaTek Inc., sometimes informally abbreviated as MTK, is a Taiwanese fabless semiconductor company that designs and markets a range of semiconductor products, providing chips for wireless communications, high-definition television, handheld mobile devices like smartphones and tablet computers, navigation systems, consumer multimedia products and digital subscriber line services as well as optical disc drives.

about: ams OSRAM is an Austrian-German photonics and sensor company formed when ams AG acquired OSRAM in 2020, based in Premstaetten, Austria with Munich operations. It makes LEDs, lasers, optical sensors and microsensors used in smartphones, cars (headlights, interior lighting), industrial and medical devices. Customers include automakers, Apple and other electronics firms. Revenue is about EUR 3.4bn with roughly 20,000 employees. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (AMS). B2B component maker, though the Osram name is known to consumers from lighting.

wiki.title: AMS-Osram
wiki.text: ams OSRAM AG is an Austrian semiconductor manufacturer headquartered in Premstätten, Austria with a co-headquarters in Munich, Germany. The company develops and produces intelligent sensors and emitter components.

about: Asus Global is the Singapore-based regional subsidiary of ASUSTeK Computer, the Taiwanese maker of laptops, desktops, motherboards, graphics cards, monitors, phones and gaming brand Republic of Gamers (ROG). Asus sells through retailers and online worldwide, with group revenue above $15bn. The parent is listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (2357). The input shows funding of about $2bn, likely an internal or financing figure. Very strong consumer and gamer brand, and ASUS has sponsored motorsport and esports in several markets.
cb_desc: Asus Global operates as a regional subsidiary and....

about: Emerson is a St. Louis, Missouri automation technology company supplying control systems, valves, measurement instruments, test and measurement tools (NI) and industrial software to process, hybrid and discrete manufacturers. Customers include oil and gas, chemical, power, life science and semiconductor firms in over 150 countries, with revenue near $17-18bn. Listed on the NYSE (EMR), and took full ownership of AspenTech in 2025. Mostly B2B, a long-standing engineering brand with little consumer visibility.

Applied Materials is a Santa Clara, California supplier of semiconductor and display manufacturing equipment, including deposition, etch, ion implant and inspection tools, plus services, serving chipmakers such as TSMC, Samsung and Intel. Revenue is near $28bn with about 35,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq (AMAT). B2B equipment maker, one of the world's largest in its field, with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Applied Materials
wiki.text: Applied Materials, Inc. is an American corporation that supplies equipment, services and software for the manufacture of semiconductor chips for electronics, flat panel displays for computers, smartphones, televisions, and solar products. The company also supplies equipment to produce coatings for flexible electronics, packaging and other applications. The company is headquartered in Santa Clara, California, and is the second largest supplier of semiconductor equipment in the world based on revenue behind Dutch company ASML.

about: Sony Group is a Tokyo-based Japanese conglomerate, founded in 1946, with segments in games and network services (PlayStation), music (Sony Music), pictures (Sony Pictures), electronics (Bravia TVs, Alpha cameras, Xperia phones, headphones), imaging and sensors, and financial services. Revenue is above 13 trillion yen with over 100,000 employees. Listed on Tokyo and NYSE (SONY). Customers are consumers worldwide. Very high global brand awareness, and a long-time partner of Formula 1 and sports.

wiki.title: Sony
wiki.text: Sony Group Corporation is a Japanese multinational conglomerate headquartered at the Sony City building in Minato, Tokyo. The Sony Group is a highly diversified global conglomerate with businesses spanning video games, music, film and television, consumer electronics, imaging and sensing, semiconductors, financial services and others.

about: Haier is a Qingdao, China-based home appliance maker, founded in 1984 and now part of Haier Smart Home (Shanghai, Hong Kong, Frankfurt: 600690, 6690), owning Haier, GE Appliances, Fisher & Paykel, Casarte, Candy and AQUA. Revenue is above 280 billion yuan, with products sold in more than 160 countries. Customers are consumers and builders. Very high household brand awareness worldwide, with sports sponsorship.

wiki.title: Haier
wiki.what: Chinese consumer electronics and appliance company
wiki.text: Haier Group Corporation is a Chinese multinational home appliances and consumer electronics company headquartered in Qingdao, Shandong. Its Haier Smart Home Company affiliate, of which it owns 35%, designs, develops, manufactures and sells home appliances including refrigerators, air conditioners, washing machines, dryers, and microwave ovens under the brand names Haier, Casarte, Leader, GE Appliances, Fisher & Paykel, Aqua, Candy and Evo. Its Haier Electronics Group affiliate manufactures consumer electronics such as mobile phones, computers, and televisions. Its ThundeRobot brand, founded in 2014, is focused on gaming computers and accessor

about: Gree Electric Appliances is a major Chinese maker of household and commercial air conditioners, the world's largest by volume, along with small appliances, refrigerators and industrial equipment, sold under Gree, Tosot and Kinghome. Based in Zhuhai (Crunchbase lists Hefei, Anhui, where it has a factory), with global sales in over 100 countries and revenue above CNY 200 billion. Listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (000651). Strong consumer brand in China.

wiki.title: Gree Electric
wiki.what: Chinese major appliance manufacturer headquartered in Zhuhai, Guangdong
wiki.text: GREE Electric Appliances Inc. of Zhuhai, branded as GREE is a Chinese home appliances manufacturer headquartered in Zhuhai, Guangdong province. It is the world's largest air-conditioner manufacturer. The company offers two types of air conditioners: household air conditioners and commercial air conditioners. The company also produces electric fans, water dispensers, heaters, rice cookers, air purifiers, water kettles, humidifiers and induction cookers, among other products. It distributes its products in China and abroad under the brand name GREE. The company has two joint-ventures with Daikin, Zhuhai GREE Daikin Device Co., Ltd., and Zhuhai

about: LG Electronics is a South Korean consumer electronics and appliances maker, selling TVs, OLED displays, refrigerators, washing machines, air conditioners, audio, and business solutions, plus vehicle components through its VS division and HVAC systems. Customers are consumers and businesses worldwide, with revenue of about 87 trillion won and operations in over 100 countries. Headquartered in Seoul. Listed on the Korea Exchange (066570), part of the LG Group. One of the world's best-known consumer electronics brands with heavy global sports sponsorship.

wiki.title: LG Electronics
wiki.text: LG Electronics Inc. is a South Korean multinational major appliance and consumer electronics corporation headquartered in Yeouido-dong, Seoul, South Korea. LG Electronics is a part of LG Corporation, the fourth largest chaebol in South Korea, and often considered as the pinnacle of LG Corp with the group's chemical and battery division LG Chem. It comprises four business units: Home Appliance Solution (HS), Media Entertainment Solution (MS), Vehicle Solution (VS), and Eco Solution (ES).

about: Dreame Technology is a Suzhou-based consumer electronics maker producing robotic vacuums and mops, cordless stick vacuums, hair dryers, and other smart home appliances, sold in over 100 markets, with growing premium lines. It started as a Xiaomi ecosystem supplier in 2017 under founder Yu Hao and now sells under its own brand. Crunchbase shows about $580 million in funding. Private. Rapidly growing consumer brand worldwide.

wiki.title: Dreame Technology
wiki.text: Dreame Technology, with the full name Dreame Technology Co., Ltd., also known as Dreametech, is a Chinese consumer electronics manufacturer founded by Yu Hao in 2017. Its main products include cordless vacuums, scrubbers, hair dryers, robotic lawn mowers, and robot vacuum cleaners and mops. The company specializes in the production of vacuum cleaners. In addition, it owns and operates an app called Dreamehome.

about: TCL Technology is a Chinese electronics and display group in Huizhou, Guangdong (the input shows Guangdong), parent of TCL Corporation brand-related businesses and the display maker TCL CSOT. It makes LCD and OLED panels, TVs, smartphones, appliances and also solar wafers through TCL Zhonghuan. Revenue is in the tens of billions of dollars and the shares are listed in Shenzhen. The TCL brand sells TVs in over 100 countries and is a top-three global TV brand, and TCL has sponsored sport internationally. Strong consumer awareness.
cb_desc: TCL Technology is the world's Largest consumer electronic...

wiki.title: TCL Technology
wiki.text: TCL Technology Group Corp., claimed to be an abbreviation for The Creative Life, is a Chinese partially state-owned electronics company headquartered in Huizhou, Guangdong province. TCL develops, manufactures, and sells consumer electronics like television sets, mobile phones, air conditioners, washing machines, refrigerators, and small electrical appliances. In 2010, it was the world's 25th-largest consumer electronics producer. On 7 February 2020, TCL Corporation changed its name to TCL Technology. It was the second-largest television manufacturer by market share in 2022 and 2023.

about: Brazilian industrial group from Jaragua do Sul, Santa Catarina, one of the world's largest electric motor, generator, transformer and drive makers, operating plants across Latin America, Europe, Asia and the US. Listed on B3 (WEGE3). B2B industrial manufacturer with revenue above BRL 30 billion and notable brand recognition in industry and in Brazil.

Broadcom (formerly Avago Technologies) is a San Jose, California semiconductor and infrastructure software company, making networking chips, custom AI accelerators (XPUs), broadband and wireless components, and enterprise software including VMware (acquired 2023) and CA. Customers include Apple, Google, hyperscalers and enterprises. Revenue is over $50 billion. Listed on Nasdaq (AVGO) with a market value above $1 trillion. B2B, with strong investor visibility and low consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Broadcom
wiki.text: Broadcom Inc. is an American multinational designer, developer, manufacturer, and global supplier of a wide range of semiconductor and infrastructure software products. Broadcom's product offerings serve the data center, networking, software, broadband, wireless, storage, and industrial markets. As of 2026, Broadcom is one of the largest companies globally.

about: Kioxia is a Tokyo memory chip maker, formerly Toshiba Memory, the inventor of NAND flash, which sells flash memory and SSDs to data center, smartphone and PC customers through its fab joint venture with Western Digital in Yokkaichi and Kitakami. Bain Capital led its 2018 purchase from Toshiba. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (285A) since December 2024. Mainly B2B but recognised in the technology industry.

wiki.title: Kioxia
wiki.text: Kioxia is a Japanese semiconductor memory and data-storage group headquartered in Tokyo. It is headed by the publicly traded holding company Kioxia Holdings Corporation. Its wholly owned principal operating subsidiary, Kioxia Corporation, develops, manufactures and sells NAND flash memory, solid-state drives (SSDs), and related storage products.

about: Corsair Gaming is a Milpitas, California maker of PC gaming and streaming hardware, including memory (Vengeance), power supplies, cases, cooling, keyboards, mice, headsets and the Elgato stream decks and capture devices. Customers are gamers and PC builders, sold through retailers and online, with annual revenue near 1.4 billion dollars. It is listed on Nasdaq (CRSR), majority owned by EagleTree Capital. It is a well known gaming brand, sponsoring esports teams and events.

Chint Electrics is the Zhejiang-based unit of Chint Group, one of China's largest makers of low-voltage electrical equipment such as circuit breakers, contactors, relays, meters and transformers. Based in Yueqing, near Wenzhou. Customers are utilities, builders, industry and distributors in more than 100 countries. Listed in Shanghai (601877). Mainly B2B, though the group has solar and energy storage units and sponsorship activity.

NortonLifeLock was the consumer cyber safety company behind Norton antivirus, LifeLock identity theft protection and later Avast, AVG and Avira, headquartered in Tempe, Arizona. It was renamed Gen Digital in 2022 after merging with Avast, and is listed on Nasdaq (GEN). It sells subscriptions to hundreds of millions of consumers, with revenue of about $4 billion. Norton is one of the best-known consumer security brands worldwide.

wiki.title: Gen Digital
wiki.text: Gen Digital Inc. is a multinational software company co-headquartered in Tempe, Arizona, United States, and Prague, Czech Republic. The company provides cybersecurity software, financial technology, and services. Gen is a Fortune 500 company and a member of the S&P 500 stock-market index. It is listed on the NASDAQ and Prague Stock Exchange. Its portfolio includes Norton, Avast, LifeLock, Avira, AVG, ReputationDefender, MoneyLion and CCleaner.

about: ASML is a Dutch semiconductor equipment company, based in Veldhoven, listed on Euronext Amsterdam and Nasdaq (ASML), and the sole supplier of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines used to make the most advanced microchips. Customers are chipmakers including TSMC, Samsung and Intel, who pay hundreds of millions of euros per machine. It has about 44,000 employees and revenue of around 28-30 billion euros. Founded in 1984 as a Philips joint venture. Hugely important B2B company with little consumer brand recognition.

wiki.title: ASML
wiki.text: ASML Holding N.V. is a Dutch multinational technology company that develops and manufactures photolithography machines used to produce integrated circuits. It is the largest supplier to the semiconductor industry and, as of 2026, the world's only manufacturer of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines, which are required to manufacture the most advanced semiconductor chips. As of January 2026, ASML had a market capitalization of approximately $527 billion, making it Europe's largest technology company and one of its most valuable companies overall.

about: Segway-Ninebot makes personal transportation products such as electric kick scooters, self-balancing scooters, e-bikes, mopeds and robots. Segway was acquired by China's Ninebot in 2015 with Xiaomi involvement, and the combined group (Beijing-based, listed on Shanghai's STAR market) sells to consumers and to sharing operators and delivery fleets worldwide, with a US base in Plano, Texas. It is a global consumer mobility brand with strong awareness in scooters and personal mobility.

Stanley Electric is a Tokyo based Japanese manufacturer of automotive lighting, such as headlamps, tail lamps and LED lighting units, as well as LEDs and displays for other uses. It is listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (6923), has revenue of about 400 billion yen, and sells to major car makers such as Honda. B2B supplier with limited consumer awareness, though known in automotive circles.

wiki.title: Stanley Electric
wiki.text: Stanley Electric Co., Ltd. (スタンレー電気株式会社; Sutanrē Denki Kabushiki-gaisha) is a Japanese manufacturer of electric lights. Stanley has 36 consolidated subsidiaries, three associated companies, 67 factories and offices in 18 countries, and over 16,000 employees.

about: Insta360 is a consumer imaging brand, 360-degree and action camera maker founded in 2015 by Arashi Vision in Shenzhen, China, with a major US presence in Los Angeles. Its products include the X series 360 cameras, Ace Pro action cameras, GO tiny cameras and Flow gimbals, sold online and through retailers in many countries to creators, travellers and sports enthusiasts. Revenue runs into the billions of yuan. Arashi Vision listed on the Shanghai STAR Market in 2025. Strong sports and creator brand awareness, directly competing with GoPro.

wiki.title: Insta360
wiki.text: Arashi Vision Inc., doing business as Insta360, is a Chinese camera and imaging technology company headquartered in Shenzhen, China with offices in Los Angeles, Tokyo and Berlin. It produces action cameras, 360-degree cameras, and stereoscopic 180-degree cameras, as well as video editing software for mobile and desktop platforms. Its products are used in action sports, travel recording, and other outdoor video applications. It has collaborated with Leica Camera on imaging technology, including action cameras such as the Insta360 Ace Pro series.

about: Ningbo Joyson Electronic is a Chinese automotive electronics and safety components group, based in Ningbo, which makes steering wheels, airbags, seat belts, infotainment and driver-assist electronics. It acquired the US airbag maker Key Safety Systems in 2016, forming Joyson Safety Systems, and supplies global carmakers. Listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (600699). Crunchbase shows about 180 million yuan of funding, dated 2015. B2B auto supplier with little consumer brand awareness.

Roborock is a Beijing-based Chinese maker of robot vacuum cleaners and mops, plus handheld wet-dry vacuums and robotic lawn products, sold under its own brand in more than 100 countries and previously made for Xiaomi's Mi Home ecosystem. Founded in 2014, it is listed on the Shanghai STAR Market (688169). Customers are households buying through retailers and online platforms. Crunchbase shows about 28 million dollars of funding, dated 2018. Strong consumer electronics brand, one of the global leaders in robot vacuums.

wiki.title: Roborock
wiki.text: Beijing Roborock Technology Co. Ltd., branded as Roborock, is a Chinese consumer goods company known for its robotic sweeping and mopping devices and handheld cordless stick vacuums.

about: Acer is a Taiwanese multinational hardware and electronics company based in Taipei, one of the world's largest PC makers, selling laptops, desktops, monitors and gaming products under the Acer, Predator and Chromebook brands. Listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (2353), with revenue near 7 to 8 billion dollars. Founded in 1976. Customers are consumers, businesses and schools in over 160 countries. Global consumer technology brand with experience of sports and esports sponsorship.
flags: last funding 2012: check it is still independent and operating

wiki.title: Acer Inc.
wiki.text: Acer Inc. is a New Taipei City-based Taiwanese multinational company that produces computer hardware and electronics, headquartered in Xizhi District. Its products include desktop PCs, laptop PCs, tablets, servers, storage devices, virtual reality devices, displays, smartphones, televisions and peripherals, as well as gaming PCs and accessories under its Predator brand. As of 2024, Acer is the world's sixth-largest personal computer vendor by unit sales.

about: Tyco Electronics Group was the electronic components business spun out of Tyco International in 2007, now known as TE Connectivity (NYSE: TEL). It designs and makes connectors, sensors and harnesses for cars, industrial equipment, aerospace, medical devices, and telecom and data networks, with roughly 85,000 employees and revenue of about 16 billion dollars. The group is domiciled in Switzerland and has legal links to Ireland. The funding shown is a 2007 note issue. B2B supplier with little consumer awareness.
flags: last funding 2007: check it is still independent and operating

wiki.title: TE Connectivity
wiki.text: TE Connectivity plc is an Irish-incorporated multinational company that designs and manufactures electrical connectors, sensors and other electronic components. Its products are used in the automotive, aerospace, defence, medical and energy industries, as well as industrial automation and data centers.

about: Sembcorp Industries is a Singapore-listed energy and urban solutions group (SGX: U96), providing power, renewable energy, integrated urban development and water services. Its businesses include thermal and renewable power in Singapore, India, China, the UK and the Middle East, plus industrial parks in Vietnam and Indonesia. Temasek Holdings, Singapore's state investment company, is a major shareholder. Revenue is in the billions of Singapore dollars. It is a B2B and utility brand, well known in Asian business but not a consumer product name.

wiki.title: Sembcorp
wiki.what: Energy and urban development company in Singapore
wiki.text: Sembcorp Industries is a Singaporean state-owned energy and urban development company.

about: E.ON is an Essen-based German energy group and Europe's largest operator of electricity distribution networks, also selling power, gas and energy solutions to tens of millions of customers in Germany, the UK, the Netherlands, Sweden, Italy, Romania and elsewhere. Revenue is about EUR 80bn with over 70,000 employees. Listed in Frankfurt (EOAN) in the DAX. Familiar consumer utility brand in Germany and a sponsor of football and other sports, including its E.ON Cup partnerships.

wiki.title: E.ON
wiki.text: E.ON SE is a German multinational electric utility company based in Essen, Germany. It operates as one of the world's largest investor-owned electric utility service providers. The name originates from the Latin word aeon, derived from the Greek αἰών aion, which means age or "infinity", with the period being added to create secondary meanings of "energy" (E) and "illumination" (ON). The company is a component of the DAX stock index.

about: Vodafone Group is a London-headquartered telecom operator, offering mobile, broadband, TV and enterprise connectivity in Europe and Africa, including Vodafone Germany, Vodafone UK (merged with Three), Vodacom in South Africa and the M-Pesa mobile money service. Revenue is about EUR 37bn. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (VOD) and Nasdaq. Very recognisable consumer brand, and a former Formula 1 sponsor (McLaren, 2001-2013), now a sponsor in sports and arts.

wiki.title: Vodafone
wiki.text: Vodafone Group plc is a British multinational telecommunications company. Its registered office and global headquarters are in Newbury, Berkshire, England. Founded in 1984 as a subsidiary of Racal Electronics, it launched the United Kingdom's second cellular network on 1 January 1985 and was demerged from Racal in 1991. Under Chris Gent, it became a global group through its merger with the American operator AirTouch in 1999 and the hostile takeover of Germany's Mannesmann in 2000, then the largest corporate merger ever. In 2013, it sold its 45% stake in Verizon Wireless to Verizon Communications for $130 billion.
